content.rationale: Nothing fixes the file's contents: the markers and the position need shapes before any implementation can read or write them. Field-for-field mirror of the recorded marker state — markers and pos — with each marker its kind, the change it targeted, its kept entry ids and the reverts recorded against it. Entries and reverts are opaque hex strings: op-log ids for a change-level operation and the journal entry id for a recording, dispatched by kind (D8c, kmmowvkw); the shape does not change between them. The position is the linear cursor (kpptprql): how many markers are applied, always within 0..=length. Closed objects keep the file markers-and-position alone; the cross-field `0 <= pos <= length` rule stays with the model invariants and the marker guards. The document carries an absolute `$id` (`urn:deccy:schema:markers`), as the node schema does, because the validator compiles a schema only under an absolute identifier (I1-schema). The schema is the one the binary carries (I1-schema-embed). A marker names the change its operation acted on, so `target` is required and non-empty (`^[a-z]+$`). No structural schema change accompanies the journal: only what an entry id means changes.
